questions.text: Ovarian germ cell tumors (OGCTs) arise from which of the following ovarian cells?

choices.A: Cells that form the ovarian connective tissue stroma
choices.B: Cells lining the surface epithelium of the ovary
choices.C: Primitive germ cells that represent the ovary’s earliest reproductive cells
choices.D: Cells responsible for hormone production within the ovary

questions.text: Which age group is most commonly affected by ovarian germ cell tumors?

choices.D: Adolescents and young females younger than 20 years old

questions.text: A nurse is reviewing the clinical characteristics of ovarian germ cell tumors. In most patients diagnosed with OGCTs, the tumor typically involves:

choices.B: Multiple cystic lesions affecting both ovaries
choices.D: The ovaries and fallopian tubes at the same time

questions.text: The occurrence of early puberty in some patients with ovarian germ cell tumors is most likely caused by the early production of which hormone?
Since ovarian germ cell tumors cannot be completely prevented, which of the following is the most appropriate measure individuals can take for early detection and health monitoring?

choices.A: Avoid all high-fat foods and processed meals
choices.C: Take hormonal supplements regularly without prescription
choices.D: Visit a doctor regularly for health monitoring and early detection

questions.text: A client in the community asks the nurse about the symptoms of having elevated cholesterol levels. Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?

choices.A: Elevated cholesterol usually causes chest pain and shortness of breath.
choices.B: Elevated cholesterol commonly causes dizziness and palpitations.
choices.C: Elevated cholesterol usually does not cause symptoms and is often detected through cholesterol testing.
choices.D: Elevated cholesterol usually presents with swelling of the legs and fatigue.

questions.text: The nurse explains the common risk factors for cardiovascular disease among Filipinos. Which of the following is NOT included among these recognized risk factors?
The nurse discusses the goal of treatment for patients diagnosed with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. Which of the following best describes the primary goal of treatment?

choices.A: To completely eliminate cholesterol production in the liver
choices.C: To achieve target LDL-C levels according to the patient’s cardiovascular risk profile
choices.D: To increase HDL levels only regardless of LDL levels

questions.text: According to treatment recommendations, statin therapy for primary prevention is recommended for individuals without clinical ASCVD who meet which of the following criteria?

choices.A: Age 30 years and above with LDL-C greater than 100 mg/dL
choices.B: Age 40 years and above regardless of cholesterol level
choices.C: Age 45 years and above with two or more risk factors and LDL-C greater than 130 mg/dL
choices.D: Any age with normal cholesterol level but with mild obesity

questions.text: A client asks the nurse about dietary practices that can help prevent or control cardiovascular disease. Which of the following correctly describes the Pinggang Pinoy method recommended for a healthy diet?

choices.A: One-half carbohydrates, one-fourth vegetables, and one-fourth meat
choices.B: One-half vegetables, one-fourth protein-rich foods such as meat, and one-fourth fiber-rich carbohydrates
choices.C: One-half meat, one-fourth vegetables, and one-fourth carbohydrates
choices.D: One-third vegetables, one-third meat, and one-third carbohydrates

questions.text: Botulism is a rare but serious illness caused by toxins produced by Clostridium botulinum. Which of the following is NOT a recognized form of botulism in humans?
A nurse explains that toxins released by Clostridium botulinum can weaken or paralyze muscles of the tongue and pharynx. Which cranial nerves are primarily affected by this toxin?

A client who consumed improperly preserved food asks the nurse how long symptoms of foodborne botulism usually take to appear. Which statement correctly describes the usual incubation period of botulism?

choices.A: Symptoms usually appear within 1–2 hours after ingestion.
choices.B: Symptoms usually appear within 2–4 days only.
choices.C: Symptoms usually appear within 12–36 hours after ingestion
choices.D: Symptoms usually appear after 10–14 days of exposure.

questions.text: During a health teaching session, the nurse explains measures to prevent botulism in the community. Which of the following practices is most appropriate to prevent botulism, particularly among infants?

choices.A: Introduce honey early to strengthen the infant’s immunity.
choices.B: Boil honey before feeding it to infants.
choices.D: Mix honey with milk before feeding it to infants.

questions.text: A patient is suspected of having foodborne botulism after consuming improperly preserved food. Which of the following interventions is recommended as part of the initial management?

choices.B: Administration of emetics and gastric lavage
choices.C: Restriction of oral fluids for 24 hours
choices.D: Administration of antihistamines to reduce allergic reaction

questions.text: A farmer in the community develops an itchy lesion on the foot after working barefoot in contaminated soil. The nurse explains that hookworm infection usually begins when:

choices.A: Hookworm eggs are inhaled and deposited in the lungs.
choices.B: Hookworm larvae are ingested directly through contaminated water.
choices.C: Hookworm larvae penetrate the skin after contact with contaminated soil.
choices.D: Hookworm parasites are transmitted through mosquito bites.

questions.text: The nurse explains the communicability of hookworm infection to community members. A person infected with hookworms can transmit the infection to others:

choices.A: Only during the first week after infection
choices.B: Only when symptoms of anemia are present
choices.C: For up to one month after treatment
choices.D: As long as the parasites remain in the gastrointestinal tract

questions.text: A nurse explains the pathophysiology of hookworm infection to a group of students. Which condition most commonly develops due to the feeding activity of hookworms in the intestinal mucosa?
A nurse is planning the care of a patient diagnosed with ancylostomiasis. Which of the following nursing interventions is INCORRECT?

choices.A: Isolation of the patient to prevent transmission
choices.B: Provide a diet high in calories, vitamins, and minerals
choices.C: Instruct the patient to maintain good personal hygiene
choices.D: Encourage the patient to use properly designated toilets and avoid open defecation

questions.text: The nurse discusses preventive measures for hookworm infection with community members. Which of the following practices help prevent ancylostomiasis?I. Proper disposal of human excretaII. Avoid walking barefoot in endemic areasIII. Maintain good personal hygieneIV. Drink untreated water from nearby streams
According to the National Statistical Coordination Board (NSCB), how is a family generally defined?

choices.A: A group of individuals living in the same community sharing common resources
choices.B: A group of persons usually living together composed of the head and persons related by blood, marriage, or adoption
choices.C: A group of individuals connected through social relationships regardless of residence
choices.D: Individuals related only by blood who share the same household

questions.text: In community health nursing, the family is considered the unit of service primarily because:

choices.A: Families are responsible for their own medical treatment
choices.B: Health problems affecting one member may influence the entire family unit
choices.C: Families usually live in the same household
choices.D: Family members have the same genetic characteristics

questions.text: Sociologists commonly define the family as:

choices.A: A legal contract between individuals living together
choices.B: A social unit interacting with the larger society
choices.C: A biological unit sharing common ancestry
choices.D: A group formed solely by marriage

questions.text: Some modern definitions describe the family as individuals joined together primarily by:

choices.C: Emotional closeness and shared identity as a family

questions.text: Based on contemporary definitions used in community health nursing, which of the following does NOT possess the essential characteristics that define a family?

choices.A: A group of individuals living in the same boarding house who share accommodation
choices.B: A married couple with children living in the same household
choices.C: Two or more persons joined by emotional bonds who identify themselves as part of a family
choices.D: A homosexual couple living together in a committed relationship

questions.text: According to the Family Code of the Philippines, marriage is defined as:

choices.A: A civil partnership between two consenting adults
choices.B: A special contract of permanent union between a man and a woman
choices.C: A temporary legal agreement between partners
choices.D: A union formed through community recognition

questions.text: In the Philippine context, same-sex marriage is currently:

choices.D: Not legally accepted under the Family Code

questions.text: In family health nursing, the concept of the “ripple effect” refers to:

choices.A: The spread of infectious diseases in a household
choices.B: Emotional reactions to stressful family events
choices.C: Changes in one family member affecting the entire family system
choices.D: The gradual development of chronic illness in families

questions.text: During a family assessment, a nurse identifies a health problem in one member and evaluates risks for other members. This process is referred to as:
A nurse performing family health nursing should assess:

choices.A: Only the sick member of the family
choices.D: Both individual members and the family unit as a whole

questions.text: In family nursing practice, theoretical frameworks are important because they help the nurse to:

choices.A: Replace the need for family assessment
choices.B: Organize observations, guide inquiry, and apply the nursing process in family care
choices.C: Eliminate the need for collaboration with the family
choices.D: Focus only on the health problems of individual family members

questions.text: According to Family Systems Theory, the family is best described as:

choices.A: A collection of individuals functioning independently
choices.B: A living social system composed of interrelated and interdependent members
choices.C: A group of individuals connected only through genetic relationships
choices.D: A temporary unit formed for economic support

questions.text: In Family Systems Theory, when a change occurs in one member of the family, the most likely outcome is that:

choices.A: Only the affected member experiences the consequences
choices.B: The change remains limited to the immediate relationship involved
choices.C: The entire family system experiences adjustments or changes

questions.text: The Interactional Approach or Symbolic Interactional Framework views the family primarily as:

choices.A: A biological system regulated by genetic factors
choices.B: A unity of interacting personalities whose behaviors are shaped by shared meanings
choices.C: A legal institution governed by social policies
choices.D: A group of individuals organized primarily by economic roles

questions.text: According to the Family Health Tasks Perspective, which of the following is one of the essential health tasks performed by the family to maintain wellness?

choices.A: Limiting the family’s interaction with community health services
choices.B: Avoiding involvement in decision-making regarding health problems
choices.C: Recognizing the presence of a health condition or problem within the family
choices.D: Delegating all health responsibilities to health professionals

questions.text: When the nurse notes that the family is unsure whether the father’s hypertension is a serious condition, which family health task is most likely not being fulfilled?

choices.A: Providing care to the sick member
choices.C: Recognizing the presence of a health problem

questions.text: The nurse observes that the family has not yet decided whether to bring the father to the health center for consultation. Which family health task is the family struggling to accomplish?

choices.A: Making decisions regarding appropriate health action
choices.B: Maintaining a home environment conducive to health
choices.D: Providing nursing care to the sick member

questions.text: The eldest daughter reminds the father to rest and attempts to assist in his daily care. This behavior demonstrates which family health task?

choices.A: Recognizing the presence of a health condition
choices.B: Providing care to a sick or dependent family member

questions.text: During the visit, the nurse notes that the family lives in a poorly ventilated and crowded home environment. Which family health task should the nurse help the family improve?

choices.B: Providing nursing care to sick members
choices.C: Maintaining a home environment conducive to health and personal development

questions.text: The nurse informs the Santos family that they can obtain free consultation and medications at the barangay health center. Which family health task is the nurse encouraging the family to perform?

choices.A: Recognizing the presence of a health problem
choices.B: Providing direct nursing care to a sick member
choices.D: Utilizing available community resources for health care

questions.text: Which Republic Act mandated the devolution of basic health services from the national government to local government units (LGUs), resulting in the establishment of local health boards?
The cooperative network formed by the municipalities in the situation to coordinate health services within a defined geographic area is known as:
Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of establishing the Inter-Local Health Zone in the situation?

choices.A: To centralize all health services under the national government
choices.B: To improve population health, ensure access to quality care, and promote efficient use of health resources
choices.C: To replace municipal health offices with provincial hospitals
choices.D: To create a new political district for health administration

questions.text: Which of the following facilities in an Inter-Local Health Zone typically serves as the central or core referral hospital?
Which of the following is NOT considered a component of an Inter-Local Health Zone (ILHZ)?

choices.A: Defined population within a geographical boundary
choices.B: Network of health facilities such as RHUs and BHSs
choices.C: Health workers from government and private sectors

questions.text: Which law contains provisions on health, safety, and welfare benefits for employees, including the requirement for companies with more than 50 workers to provide the services of a full-time nurse?
When Maria conducted an orientation for newly hired workers about workplace hazards and safety practices, which occupational health nursing function was she primarily performing?
During her volunteer work in the school, Maria conducted height and weight measurements and screening for possible health problems among students. Which school nursing activity does this represent?

choices.B: Health and nutrition assessment, screening, and case finding

questions.text: Which of the following laws is considered a major legal basis for school nursing practice, focusing on the welfare and protection of children and youth?
Which of the following BEST explains why most school nursing activities focus on health promotion and disease prevention rather than treatment?

choices.A: Schools are not allowed to treat sick students
choices.B: Most pupils in school are generally well, so emphasis is placed on prevention and health promotion
choices.C: School nurses are not trained to manage illnesses
choices.D: Schools do not have clinic facilities

questions.text: Nurse Angela observed that when one member becomes ill, other members adjust their roles and behaviors to support the sick member. Which principle of the Family Systems Theory does this illustrate?

choices.B: A change in one part of the system results in changes in the entire system

questions.text: When Nurse Angela focused on how family members communicate, make decisions, resolve conflicts, and interpret interactions, which theoretical framework was she primarily applying?
When the nurse analyzed the family’s stage of development and the adjustments required in raising children while caring for an elderly member, which theoretical perspective was being applied?
When Nurse Angela assessed the roles of each family member, communication patterns, and power structure within the family, she was applying which perspective?
According to the Structural-Functional model, which of the following is NOT one of the four structural dimensions of the family?
In Denham’s Family Health Model, the emotional bond between family members is referred to as:
When family members cooperatively share resources, skills, and information to promote the health of the family, which functional process in Denham’s Family Health Model is demonstrated?
Family routines such as dietary habits, hygiene practices, sleep patterns, and physical activity fall under which category of Denham’s family routines?
According to the Family Health Tasks Perspective, which of the following is the first health task that the family must perform?

choices.A: Utilize community resources for health care
choices.B: Provide care to the sick member
choices.D: Recognize the presence of a health condition or problem

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the health tasks of the family necessary to maintain and promote health according to the Family Health Tasks Perspective?

choices.A: Establish political leadership in the community
choices.B: Utilize community resources for health care
choices.C: Develop economic independence of the family
choices.D: Maintain social prestige in the community

questions.text: Which phase of the nursing process was Nurse Lea performing when she gathered and analyzed information about the Ramos family?
Nursing assessment in family health nursing primarily aims to determine which of the following?

choices.A: The treatment plan for each sick family member
choices.B: The family’s status as a client and its ability to maintain wellness and resolve health problems
choices.C: The physician’s diagnosis of diseases within the family
choices.D: The financial capability of the family to pay for hospital services

questions.text: Which of the following is the end result of the nursing assessment process in family nursing practice?
When Nurse Lea compared the health status of family members with standards of personal, social, and environmental health, she was performing which type of assessment?
Which of the following health conditions may be identified during first-level assessment?

choices.A: Family’s inability to provide care for the sick
choices.B: Failure to utilize community health services
choices.C: Wellness states, health threats, health deficits, and stress points
choices.D: Barriers to performing family health tasks

questions.text: Which type of assessment identifies the reasons or barriers for the family’s inability to perform health tasks related to a specific health condition?
Which of the following is considered one of the five types of data collected during first-level assessment?

choices.A: Physician’s diagnosis of each family member
choices.D: Nursing care plan of the family

questions.text: When Nurse Lea grouped related information together to determine relationships among data, which step in data analysis was she performing?
When the nurse drew conclusions about the possible causes of the family’s health problems, which step in data analysis was being performed?
According to the typology of nursing problems in family health care, a family nursing problem is primarily stated as:

choices.A: A medical condition of a family member
choices.B: An inability of the family to perform a specific health task and the reasons for it
choices.C: A list of health services needed by the family
choices.D: A description of the family’s socioeconomic status

questions.text: Which law provides the basis for the practice of nursing including nursing care during conception, labor, delivery and infancy?
Prenatal care is BEST defined as:

choices.C: Care given during labor and delivery

questions.text: According to WHO standards, the minimum recommended number of prenatal visits during pregnancy is:
A pregnant woman with multiple risk factors should:

choices.A: Maintain the same number of prenatal visits
choices.B: Delay consultation until the third trimester
choices.D: Seek care only when symptoms appear

questions.text: According to national survey data, most prenatal care in the Philippines is provided by:
Which medication should the nurse expect the physician to order for Ana?
Ana reports a history of penicillin allergy. What is the most appropriate management?
The nurse explains that untreated maternal syphilis can affect the fetus because:

choices.A: The organism multiplies only in the placenta
choices.B: The organism can cross the placenta
choices.C: The infection remains limited to the cervix

questions.text: Ana asks if she needs a cesarean section because of her infection. What is the best response by the nurse?

choices.A: Cesarean delivery is mandatory for mothers with syphilis
choices.C: Mode of delivery is based on obstetric indications
choices.D: Cesarean delivery is required to prevent transmission

questions.text: Which additional intervention is essential to prevent reinfection and protect the pregnancy?

choices.A: Isolation of the mother after treatment
choices.C: Evaluation and treatment of sexual partner(s)

questions.text: The government goal is for 80% of women to receive the first postpartum visit within:
According to DOH standards, postpartum visits should ideally occur:

choices.A: Immediately after delivery and at 6 months
choices.B: Within two days after delivery and again one month after

questions.text: Which micronutrient should be given immediately after delivery or within one month postpartum?
Iron supplementation during the postpartum period should include:
When Nurse Mia assesses and manages postpartum problems such as mastitis or cracked nipples, she is performing which nursing responsibility?
The recommended feeding for infants during the first six months of life is:
Which breastfeeding indicator suggests that the infant is feeding effectively?
An infant who feeds for 5–10 minutes on each breast demonstrates:
When the nurse evaluates maternal knowledge using a scale from 1 (no knowledge) to 5 (substantial knowledge), she is applying which framework?
Nursing interventions that are initiated by the nurse based on a nursing diagnosis and judgement are known as:
Which characteristic of the study best identifies it as participatory action research?

choices.A: Data were collected by trained epidemiologists
choices.B: Families served mainly as respondents to structured questionnaires
choices.C: Community members participated as partners in identifying problems
choices.D: The study focused only on laboratory confirmation of malaria cases

questions.text: During the study, families shared their experiences of helplessness and lack of access to health services. What research purpose does this primarily serve?

choices.C: Exploring the lived experiences of the participants

questions.text: The nurse researcher guided families through stages of behavior change such as constructing intention, translating intention to action, and integrating the change into lifestyle. Which theoretical framework guided this process?
Which outcome BEST indicates that family empowerment in malaria prevention was achieved?

choices.A: Increased dependence on government spraying programs
choices.B: More reliance on barangay health workers for vector control
choices.C: Families independently organized stream-cleaning activities near their homes

questions.text: The modification of stream cleaning from a large village activity to a household cluster approach primarily addressed which research consideration?

During protocol development, the nurse researcher organized a community advisory board composed of barangay leaders and family representatives to review the research procedures and consent process. Which research principle is BEST demonstrated by this strategy?

The study used repeated cycles of problem identification, action, reflection, and modification of interventions during the malaria control program.Which research design BEST describes this methodological approach?

During data analysis, the nurse-researcher combined epidemiologic data on malaria incidence with qualitative narratives from family discussions about mosquito breeding practices. Which methodological approach is MOST consistent with this strategy?

To evaluate sustainability of the intervention, the researchers measured mosquito larval density, malaria case detection rates, and frequency of community vector-control activities over time. Which research concept is BEST represented by these indicators?

A nurse researcher plans to translate the successful malaria empowerment model into national malaria control programs through policy recommendations and health system implementation. Which type of research BEST describes this process?
